processingNote: Asset Recovery Wave 3 (2026-08-18): material-factor-edit derivative addressing the CONDITIONAL-for-material-fault glass vessels (docs/assets/reviews/chemistry-reactions-visual.md), which render as near-black opaque silhouettes under the app's no-IBL two-directional-light stage. Edited only the 'chemistry_set_glass' material (37 node instances: beakers, bottles, graduated cylinder) via a small @gltf-transform/core script: metallicFactor 1 -> 0.05, roughnessFactor 1 -> 0.35, per the review's own scoped recommendation ('remap the glass nodes' metalness factor down toward 0 and rely on diffuse/normal map plus modest roughness'). The 'chemistry_set' material (non-glass props: clamp stand, tripod, tube rack, etc., which the review found render correctly already) was left untouched. No geometry, texture pixels, node transforms, or license/attribution facts changed -- verified by re-reading the material factors back out of the written .glb. Original file preserved unmodified alongside this derivative.

validation.notes: File size effectively unchanged (small delta from JSON re-serialization, not from any resampling). This is a scalar-factor edit only; the baked metallicRoughnessTexture pixels are unchanged, so final per-pixel metalness/roughness = factor x texture value as per the glTF PBR spec. Flagged for a follow-up visual-acceptance render pass to confirm the glass vessels now read as translucent/frosted rather than near-black under the app's actual GenericViewer lighting rig.

note: Whole-diorama lab-bench scene; individual prop splitting (beaker/test-tube/clamp-stand as separate hero assets) remains a separate, unaddressed follow-up idea per the source review, not attempted here.
